title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a retrospective, self-critical summary (numbered points 1°, 2°, 3°) of the long computation in 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets'. Its object, M~_{0,3}, is a group (or group-scheme-like object) of automorphisms or 'multiplications' attached to the profinite fundamental group of M_{0,3} = P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, of Grothendieck–Teichmüller type. M~_{0,3}[0] is the part adapted to the (tangential) base point 0. M~_{0,3}(0) is a subgroup described by 'multiplications μ'.

The previous page gives semi-direct decompositions: (44) M~[0] ≅ M~(0)·L_0π and (45) M~ ≅ M~(0)·S^{+∧}_{0,3}. It also states that the operation Θ_G^π coincides with Θ_{B'_0}^π on M~[0] and reduces to i_{T_0}(μ) on M~(0).

Point 2°, concluded here: Θ_G^π (the object U) was built 'by sheer force' through Θ_{B'_0}^π (the object u). This caused a long confusion between u and U, made worse because Grothendieck mostly worked in M~[0]. He says that, after fumbling with unsuitable points of view, he found M~[0] to be technically the most elegant framework from §45 on. He says the confusion was cleared up only 'yesterday and today'.

Point 3°: the laws (35), (36), presumably composition or transformation laws, were obtained only by working thoroughly with parameters a, b attached to u. It suffices to work in M~[0] and to define two maps:
- u ↦ a, from M~[0] to T_ρ(Ẑ)/±1;
- u ↦ b, from M~[0] to N'_σ(Ẑ)/±1.
The next page adds that these maps are made trivial on L_0Π̂.

Here ρ and σ are very plausibly the elliptic generators of order 3 and 2 of PSL_2(Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3. In that reading:
- T_ρ is the centralizer torus of ρ in SL_2, so T_ρ(Ẑ) is the norm-one units of Ẑ[ζ_3].
- N'_σ is a variant (normalizer or derived) of the torus attached to σ, built on Ẑ[i].

So a and b would record how an element of M~ acts, up to sign, at the two orbifold points j=1728 and j=0 of M_{1,1}. This reading fits the next page's programme: interpret a, b by class field theory of the quadratic fields Q(j) (j a cube root of unity) and a second field written Q(j'), perhaps Q(i). It also fits the next page's plan to interpret them via maps and dessins tied to quotients of SL_2(Z)^. The overall problem is the explicit description of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group through its action on the profinite modular/braid tower, with local invariants at the elliptic points.
errors: No mathematical claim is checkable on this page; it is a retrospective. The identification of T_ρ and N'_σ as CM tori is my interpretation, not stated explicitly by Grothendieck.

The page admits a long conceptual confusion (u vs U) that was only recently resolved, and the next page calls the understanding 'fragile'. Results from the earlier sections should be read with this in mind.

ideas.what: Working in the based version M~_{0,3}[0], adapted to the tangential base point 0, as the technically most elegant framework, with semi-direct decompositions over inner-type subgroups
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points and the GT group as a subgroup of Aut(π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}, 01→))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989) for tangential base points; Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara for GT
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and base points in spirit; the Longue Marche treats π_1 of P^1 minus 3 points

ideas.what: Parameters a ∈ T_ρ(Ẑ)/±1 and b ∈ N'_σ(Ẑ)/±1 attached to each element u, i.e. invariants of GT-type elements at the order-3 and order-2 elliptic points of SL_2(Z)
ideas.modern_name: Galois/GT action at the orbifold (CM) points of M_{1,1}; conjugators in centralizers of torsion elements of SL_2(Ẑ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura; Collas–Maugeais (GT action on torsion and inertia in M_{1,1} and M_{g,n})

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines invariants a, b of elements of his GT-type group with values in Ẑ-points of tori (mod ±1) attached to the elliptic elements ρ and σ. The next page plans to interpret them via class field theory of Q(ζ_3) and a second quadratic field, and via dessins on quotients of SL_2(Ẑ). An explicit link from GT-type parameters to class field theory of the CM fields at j=0 and j=1728 is only partially present in the literature.
missed.quote: définir u ↦ a  M~_{0,3}[0] → T_ρ(Ẑ)/±1 → N'_σ(Ẑ)/±1  u ↦ b
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could relate GT torsion and elliptic-point phenomena (Collas–Maugeais, Nakamura) to CM class field theory, an angle that is not systematically developed.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly autobiographical commentary on a confusion between two constructions. The one notable item is the introduction of torus-valued parameters a, b at the elliptic points, with a planned class-field-theoretic interpretation. That is suggestive but is only sketched here, and it overlaps with later work on GT and M_{1,1} torsion.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'entre u et Y' should read 'entre u et U' (underlined U, matching the previous page's 'U a été construit par u').
'je me résignais' reads more like 'je me résignais' / 'je m'obstinais' (uncertain); 'avec des points de vue pas convenables' is uncertain, possibly 'pas commodes'.
In 'M_{0,3}^~[0]' on line 4 the subscript may be written 'g,3' but is meant as '0,3'.
's'est définitivement dissipée que hier et aujourd'hui' is correct; the next segment is 'à force de mettre et remettre les pieds dans mes propres plats'.
The arrows in point 3°: two parallel maps from M~_{0,3}[0], to T_ρ(Ẑ)/±1 (u ↦ a, written above) and to N'_σ(Ẑ)/±1 (u ↦ b, written below), not a composite.
